title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput numbers from last run, adjust continuous batching and concurrency targets, discuss queueing/backpressure behavior and next steps for a 2-hour production-like benchmark. Action items assigned for a follow-up benchmark and security doc share.
next_steps: Redwood to run 2-hour benchmark with suggested concurrency profile and share raw logs (Raj) by 2027-05-07
Customer to validate RU budget and confirm target p95 latency threshold by 2027-05-10
Share revised benchmark spreadsheet and Grafana dashboard link (Emma) by EOD
action_items: Raj Patel — run 2-hour benchmark: continuous batching on, concurrency target 6 then 12, collect per-GPU utilization, due 2027-05-07
Lena Ortiz — provide production request distribution (qps by payload size) and SLOs, due 2027-05-10
Emma Chen — send security summary and link to benchmark spreadsheet, due 2027-05-05
transcript:
[00:00] Emma Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining on short notice, looks like we have about 45 minutes, quick roll call?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: lena here, ml infra team, good to go.
[00:11] Marcus Hale: marcus from product, thanks.
[00:14] Raj Patel: raj, se, ready.
[00:16] Ibrahim Khan: ibrahim, s-r-e, on my end.
[00:20] Emma Chen: awesome, quick agenda — review results from last night's benchmark, talk tuning knobs (continuous batching, concurrency), queueing behavior, and agree next steps.
[00:30] Raj Patel: so quick recap — we ran the test @ 200 qps sustained for 30 minutes with the current POC model v1.2, continuous batching enabled with max_batch_size 64, and concurrency set to 8 per instance.
[00:45] Marcus Hale: percentiles looked pretty good but we saw a few spikes right?
[00:50] Raj Patel: yeah we got a median token latency of about 45ms per token, p95 was 420ms, p99 spiked to 1.2s a few times. GPU utilization averaged 78% but spiky.
[01:05] Lena Ortiz: we saw queue depth growing in the ingress for ~40s windows, i think that's when the p99 blew up.
[01:12] Raj Patel: exactly — looks like concurrent requests cluster caused batching to balloon then some queueing in the request router. Continuous batching is great for amortizing kernel overhead but if arrival patterns are bursty it increases tail.
[01:25] Ibrahim Khan: can you explain continuous batching again? earlier you said it aggregates open slots until either timeout or max batch hit?
[01:33] Raj Patel: yeah so continuous batching keeps filling the batch while a request is in-flight, it uses a short accumulation window (we had 8ms) then sends; that reduces per-token cost but raises latency variance when bursts align.
[01:44] Emma Chen: tradeoff conversation — customer target is high throughput with p95 < 500ms. Marcus, is that still the product target?
[01:52] Marcus Hale: yes p95 500ms is the threshold for launch, lower is better. Cost target is also important, we can't scale GPUs out indefinitely.
[01:59] Raj Patel: proposed next tuning — lower accumulation window from 8ms to 4ms, reduce max_batch_size to 48 for this workload, and target concurrency 6 per instance then scale to 12 for stress test. That should trim p99 spikes and smooth queueing.
[02:13] Lena Ortiz: curious how that affects throughput — will smaller batches increase per-token cost a lot?
[02:18] Raj Patel: small increase — we expect ~6-9% token-cost increase at steady state but p95 improves; plus a smarter autoscale policy and request routing can keep cost in check by pushing to spare capacity when queues form.
[02:30] Ibrahim Khan: the other issue we saw is prefix cache hits — during the run cache hit rate dropped to 22% for the 512 token prefix set, probably because our queries were high variance.
[02:40] Raj Patel: yeah low KV cache hit reduces batching benefit too. We recommended a short-lived prefix caching TTL and exploring deduping at the client to raise hit rates.
[02:48] Marcus Hale: is there a way to throttle on the client side to avoid bursts? we can smooth requests but don't want to add latency at product layer.
[02:55] Emma Chen: typical pattern is token-bucket rate shaping with a small leaky-bucket smoothing to avoid microbursts — that usually fixes the queueing without visible product impact.
[03:05] Lena Ortiz: ok we'll try smoothing on our side but still want Redwood to run another benchmark to show impact.
[03:10] Raj Patel: agreed — i'll run a 2-hour benchmark in staging that mimics NovaPay traffic (we have the sample distribution you sent) with two profiles: profile A concurrency 6, accumulation 4ms; profile B concurrency 12, accumulation 6ms. We'll collect per-request latencies, batch sizes, GPU util, and queue depth.
[03:25] Marcus Hale: perfect — can you also capture burst scenario? like a 30s jump to 400 qps?
[03:30] Raj Patel: yes we'll include a burst ramp at minute 40 for 60s.
[03:34] Emma Chen: please dump logs and share the benchmark spreadsheet link, we'll annotate.
[03:38] Raj Patel: noted. Also want to mention we saw a few transient errors flagged as 502 from the ingress when concurrency hit ~18, that's likely router timeouts, not model. We should configure backpressure at 15 concurrent per instance to avoid cascading.
[03:52] Ibrahim Khan: we prefer graceful 429 over 502, so configuring queue limits + 429 backpressure would be ideal.
[03:59] Raj Patel: Redwood supports 429s via request policing in the router, will enable that for the next run.
[04:04] Emma Chen: security note — you'll want the SOC2 summary, encryption at rest details, and the KMS integration doc. I'll send links.
[04:11] Lena Ortiz: yes, send SOC2 and the VPC peering checklist. We need to review before moving to a dedicated pilot.
[04:18] Emma Chen: action items recap — raj to run benchmark and share logs/spreadsheet; lena to provide final SLOs and traffic distro; emma to send security docs and dashboard links.
[04:28] Marcus Hale: timeline — if bench results look good we aim to start dedicated pilot the week of 2027-05-17.
[04:34] Emma Chen: ok we'll tentatively plan that. any other questions?
[04:38] Lena Ortiz: can you ping about the grafana dashboard URL? i couldn't access last time.
[04:42] Emma Chen: yes i'll double-check permissions and include link in the notes.
[04:46] Raj Patel: quick note on instrumentation — we'll include per-batch kernel time and memband counters so you can see if quantization or kernel selection is the bottleneck.
[04:55] Ibrahim Khan: thanks, that will help root cause.
[04:58] Emma Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with the spreadsheet and security docs, speak soon.
[05:03] (call ends)
